newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-COMBINED PACIFIC TEAM TARGETS SUPER 12. [CORRECTED 03:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-COMBINED PACIFIC TEAM TARGETS SUPER 12. [CORRECTED 03:25 GMT]

text.p: The Pacific nations of Fiji, Tonga and Western Samoa said on Wednesday they had joined forces and would apply as one team to take part in next year's Super 12 rugby series.
Fiji and Western Samoa coaches Brad Johnstone and Bryan Williams told a press conference they had formally written to Australia, New Zealand and South Africa seeking entry into the Super 12.
The competition is currently played between five New Zealand, four South African and three Australian teams from the nations, whose rugby unions are linked through the SANZAR committee.
(Corrects from "is currently played between four clubs from each of these three nations.)
The islanders said they intended to launch a combined Pacific Islands team, involving players from around the region.
Tonga was not represented at the conference because of a current tour of South Africa, but had given support to the proposed combined team, the two coaches said

Earlier this year, All Black coach John Hart expressed doubt over a Pacific team, such as Western Samoa, entering the Super 12 because he said it was a regional competition, not an international series.
Hart said he believed the competition was working well and should not be tampered with just yet.

But Johnstone and Williams said the objective of launching a combined team was to prove the Pacific islands could work together to field a highly competitive side that would be worthy of entry into an expanded Super 12.
Rather than compete with each other for Super 12 representation, the three unions had decided to combine their efforts into one force, they said.
"The Pacific Islands team will be truly regional and therefore fits well within the Super 12 concept," they said.

The combined population of the three countries was less than one million people, which was comparable to the population bases of some of the New Zealand teams and well short of the population resources to which the South African and Australian teams had access, they added.
The islands aim to have a team fully prepared to offer warm-up matches to existing Super 12 teams by January 1998.
The logistics involved in selection, team management and administration would be worked through in the next few months, they added.
Williams said the Pacific nations had called on the three unions attending a SANZAR meeting in Auckland this week to recognise and consider the value of the islands' proposal.
He said a Pacific team would be good for the development of rugby, not just in the Pacific, but for improving its international standard.
The final of this year's Super 12 competition between the Auckland Blues and Australia's ACT Brumbies will be played at Eden Park, Auckland this Saturday, with kickoff at 0230 GMT.
